Grade: PP1
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: GOD’S
Topic 1.3: My family CREATION

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on My family CREATION. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain My family CREATION in simple words
2. give Kenyan school/community examples of My family CREATION
3. describe one responsible action linked to My family CREATION
4. show respect and fairness when practising My family CREATION

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MY FAMILY CREATION
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
My family CREATION helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: MY FAMILY CREATION
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Explain My family CREATION in simple words

What this means
In this part you learn to explain My family CREATION in simple words. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain My family CREATION in simple words.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “My family CREATION” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain My family CREATION in simple words. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give Kenyan school/community examples of My family CREATION

What this means
In this part you learn to give Kenyan school/community examples of My family CREATION. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give Kenyan school/community examples of My family CREATION.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to My family CREATION.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give Kenyan school/community examples of My family CREATION. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe one responsible action linked to My family CREATION

What this means
In this part you learn to describe one responsible action linked to My family CREATION. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe one responsible action linked to My family CREATION.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe one responsible action linked to My family CREATION. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Show respect and fairness when practising My family CREATION

What this means
In this part you learn to show respect and fairness when practising My family CREATION. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: show respect and fairness when practising My family CREATION.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “My family CREATION” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can show respect and fairness when practising My family CREATION. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what My family CREATION is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “My family CREATION” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: explain My family CREATION in simple words)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to My family CREATION. (skill: give Kenyan school/community examples of My family CREATION)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: describe one responsible action linked to My family CREATION)

Example 4: Connect “My family CREATION” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: show respect and fairness when practising My family CREATION)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach My family CREATION to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain My family CREATION in simple words.
3. Practise this skill: give Kenyan school/community examples of My family CREATION.
4. Practise this skill: describe one responsible action linked to My family CREATION.
5. Make one local Kenya example of My family CREATION from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for My family CREATION: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study My family CREATION?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

2. What is the name of members are a gift from God. sing simple songs thanking God for your guardian?
3. How many sisters do his/her parents, brothers and 20:12) you have?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what My family CREATION means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain My family CREATION in simple words.
5. Be able to: give Kenyan school/community examples of My family CREATION.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
